title: Your Phone Could Have Flown the Apollo Missions Millions of Times Over
description:
The computer that guided Apollo 11 to the Moon had a tiny fraction of the processing power of the phone in your pocket. Here's the actual comparison.

#shorts #techfacts #space

scenes.text: The computer that landed astronauts on the Moon was less powerful than a calculator you'd find in a drawer today.
The Apollo Guidance Computer ran at about one point two megahertz, with roughly seventy three kilobytes of memory total.
A modern smartphone runs at billions of operations per second, with memory measured in gigabytes, not kilobytes.
That's a difference of roughly a hundred thousand times the processing power, sitting in your pocket right now.
And yet the Apollo Guidance Computer got three separate missions safely to the lunar surface and back.
It's not really about raw power. It's that every line of that code had to work perfectly, on the first try, with no updates possible.
